pr_title: [RDG] Account of parameter name in signature comparison

issue_context.title: query parameter does not work correctly in net 8 preview 7 under native aot
issue_context.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

i cant have a route like this:
`/camera/archive/{cameraId}/chunk/{chunkName}`
to accept a request like this:
`/camera/archive/01870310-2e1e-428e-82fa-6bf15a74ecf0/chunk/4868579.ts`
because `chunkName` for some reason will always be null. this works fine if i do `dotnet run` but if i publish it with native aot, it does not work. see the attached file for the full bug repro.

i also believe this is a regression since it works fine with net 8.0 preview 6. you can try it by changing the versions in Dockerfile from 7 to 6.

### Expected Behavior

`chunkName` is not null or empty.

### Steps To Reproduce

[querybug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/files/12331399/querybug.zip)


### Exceptions (if any)

_No response_

### .NET Version

dotnet 8.0 preview 7

### Anything else?

_No response_

review_comments: Signature comparison is a whole thing.  I don't suppose roslyn exposes theirs?

Hmmm...not that I am aware of.

Although, FWIW, the signature here is contextualized to the things we care about for minimal APIs in particular (for example they account for the HTTP method associated with a request) so the Roslyn model might not be totally helpful here.
Interceptors fixed generating overloads for methods with the same signature but differing nullability so we no longer have a warning to suppress.
